newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Caretaker NZ premier reallocates portfolios.
newsitem.headline: Caretaker NZ premier reallocates portfolios.

text.p: Caretaker New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Thursday announced the reallocation of the portfolios of ministers who retired from parliament at October 12's general election.
The retiring ministers are Philip Burdon, John Falloon, Sir Robin Gray and Roger McClay.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Affairs Minister Don McKinnon will assume Burdon's responsibilities as Minister for Trade Negotiations and Associate Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Bolger said.
McKinnon will also assume the responsibilities Gray had as Minister of State, and Foreign Affairs and Trade associate minister.
Energy Minister Doug Kidd will take over Burdon's State-Owned Enterprises portfolio, responsibility for the Public Trust Office and other SOE-related responsibilities.
Falloon's portfolios of Forestry and Racing will be assigned to Denis Marshall.

McClay's portfolio of Youth Affairs is assigned to Katherine O'Regan, and his associate ministerial responsibilities in Pacific Island Affairs, Education and Social Welfare will be assumed by the relevant portfolio ministers.

Bolger also confirmed that Housing Minister Murray McCully would take over the portfolio responsibilities previously held by John Banks -- Tourism, Sport, Fitness and Leisure, Local Government and Civil Defence. Banks resigned from cabinet last week.

No government has been formed since the October 12 election where no party gained an outright majority and the cabinet reshuffle was forced on the caretaker government by a requirement that ministers who are no longer MPs relinquish their positions within 28 days of an election.
